narrative.overview:
A large, confident studio page that says who this is in one line, states its claim at the scale of a wordmark, and then asks the visitor a question. The whole system exists to make one interaction feel inevitable: you say why you came, and the page commits to that answer.

The ground is warm bone — not cool paper, not near-black. Against it, near-black ink and exactly one vermilion. Everything is enormous or quiet; there is no middle register.

Depth is drawn, not lit. No shadows, and no radii except the pills, which are fully round by rule.
keyCharacteristics: Warm bone ground with real grain, never a flat white
One vermilion, split into a text role and a display role by contrast
Anton enormous for claims; Archivo for reading; Azeret for every measured value
Every control is a pill; nothing else is round
Skim first, operate on request — no instrument opens uninvited

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion may only be applied to something that is currently changing, can change, or has just been chosen. On an inert element it is a bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Two Vermilions Rule
rules.body: The split between --signal and --signal-display is a contrast rule, not a taste one. Under 24px, or under white text, it takes --signal. There is no third vermilion.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Colour marks the choice, never the menu. An earlier build gave each lens pill its own hue, which drained the accent from the one actually chosen.

rules.name: The Measured Value Rule
rules.body: Every number a reader is meant to compare is set in Azeret Mono, tabular, and aligned.

rules.name: The Display-Is-For-Claims Rule
rules.body: Anton appears only on claims, at display or headline size. Never in a control, label, pill, or panel.

rules.name: The Skim-First Rule
rules.body: Every claim must be readable, and its proof comprehensible, without operating anything. Instruments open on request and unmount when closed.

rules.name: The Flat-Field Rule
rules.body: Separation is drawn, not lit. Adding a box-shadow to this system is a defect.

dos: Do keep exactly one accent, and spend it on what is live or chosen.
Do take --signal (#b8330d) for anything under 24px or under white text.
Do set every comparable number in Azeret Mono, tabular.
Do make every interactive control a pill at 999px.
Do let each claim read fully before anything needs operating.
Do keep the status line and the primary action in the first viewport at every width.
Do draw marks as SVG at one stroke weight.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow, or any radius between 0 and 999px.
Don't put vermilion on an inert element, or the display vermilion on small text.
Don't give the unchosen options colour.
Don't use Anton for anything but a claim.
Don't open an instrument the visitor did not ask for.
Don't number the work blocks — a declared lens re-orders them, so any fixed index becomes a lie.
Don't substitute a Unicode character for an icon.
